voice.style: Professional, warm, natural; clear English; unhurried business-presentation pace

scenes.title: Opening
screenAction: Full HD window on the home page, scrolled to the top
Hold on the hero for three seconds
Slow scroll to the first section
scenes.narration: This is Greenscape Landscaping PH, a landscaping and plant business in Palawan. Its new platform brings the public website, an online shop, an employee attendance portal and a business administration console together on one system. In the next few minutes we will walk through each part, using the running application and sample data.

scenes.title: Three portals, one system
screenAction: Title card with the three portal screenshots side by side: website, employee portal, admin console
scenes.narration: The system has three portals. Customers use the website to explore services and projects, request quotations and buy plants. Employees use a separate portal to clock in and out, check their schedule and file requests. Staff and administrators use the admin console to manage content, orders, people and settings. All three share one secure API and one sign-in service, and every permission is checked on the server.
visualDirection: Three cards slide in left to right
Highlight each card as it is named

scenes.title: Customer homepage
screenAction: Scroll the home page slowly from hero to footer
Hover the main navigation items
Pause on Gardens we have built and From our sites
scenes.narration: The homepage opens with an editorial hero and a white botanical design. As visitors scroll, sections reveal themselves with gentle, scroll-driven motion, and the page stays fully usable for visitors who prefer reduced motion. Below the hero come the four services, featured projects, a masonry wall of photos from the sites, stories from the team and client testimonials. The header keeps navigation, the quote button and the account in reach.
visualDirection: Soft zoom on the From our sites photo wall

scenes.title: Services, projects and gallery
scenes.feature: Service pages, project portfolio, masonry gallery and lightbox
screenAction: Open Services, then one service page: show packages and the before-and-after slider
Open Projects, filter by a category, open a project
Open Gallery, apply a filter, open a photo in the lightbox and step to the next
scenes.narration: Each service has its own page with maintenance packages, a before-and-after comparison and guides from the growers. The projects portfolio can be filtered by category, and every project tells its story with photographs. The gallery collects the photos in a Pinterest-style masonry layout. Visitors can filter by category or place, and open any photo in a full-screen viewer that supports swiping on phones.
visualDirection: Zoom into a gallery tile, then cut to the open lightbox

scenes.title: Shopping
scenes.feature: Catalogue, product page, cart, test checkout
screenAction: Open Shop, search and sort
Open a priced product, choose a size, Add to cart
Open the cart, change the quantity
Proceed to checkout, show the test-mode banner, pay on the test payment page
Show the order page
scenes.narration: The shop lists the nursery's plants with search, filters and sorting. A product page shows photos, sizes, live stock and care information. Signed-in customers add items to their cart and check out with delivery anywhere in Palawan, where the fee for their municipality is added. Prices and stock are checked on the server, and stock is held while the payment is pending. This environment uses a test payment provider, so the checkout shows a clear test-mode notice and no real money moves.

scenes.title: Customer account and quotations
screenAction: Open Sign in, sign in with the synthetic demo customer (email and password)
Show My account: orders and quotation status
Open Get a quote and step through the form without sending
Open Messages
scenes.narration: Customers can create an account with email and password, and Google sign-in can be switched on for each environment. The account page shows orders and quotation requests with their status. The quotation form guides customers through their project in three steps and accepts photos and plans as attachments. Customers can also message the team directly, and replies arrive in the same thread.
visualDirection: Blur the email field after typing
Step indicator callout on the quote form

scenes.title: Employee portal
screenAction: Open the employee login, sign in as the demo employee
Show the dashboard: greeting, clock card, coming-up shifts, last seven days
scenes.narration: Employees have their own portal. They do not sign up themselves: HR creates each login from the employee record, with a temporary password that must be changed on first sign-in. The dashboard greets the employee and puts the clock card first, followed by upcoming shifts, a seven-day summary and recent notifications.
visualDirection: Phone-sized window (390 px) for this scene

scenes.title: Attendance
scenes.feature: Clock in and out, attendance history, schedule
screenAction: Press Clock in; show 'Clocked in since'
Open Attendance: month calendar and day list
Open Schedule
scenes.narration: Clocking in takes one tap. The time always comes from the server, not the phone, and repeated taps count only once. The attendance page shows a month calendar and each day's record, including late arrivals, undertime and overtime worked out from the employee's schedule. The schedule page shows the shifts assigned by HR.
visualDirection: Zoom on the clock status line after the tap

scenes.title: Employee requests
screenAction: Open Requests
Start a leave request: type, dates, reason; submit
Show a correction request for a missed time-out
scenes.narration: From the requests page, employees file leave and correct missed punches. Leave is checked against the employee's balance and against overlapping requests before it is sent. A correction shows the proposed times next to what was recorded and can include a photo or document. Every decision comes back to the employee as a notification.

scenes.title: Admin dashboard
screenAction: Sign in to the admin console as the demo super admin
Show the dashboard panels
Open and close the sidebar groups
scenes.narration: The admin console is for staff. Its dashboard adapts to each person's role: a sales manager sees sales and orders, HR sees attendance and leave, and a super administrator sees everything. Panels show today's sales, items waiting for a decision, website traffic, low stock and system status, each linking to the page where the work is done.

scenes.title: Content management
screenAction: Open CMS → Services, open a service
Edit a sample sentence in the draft, save
Open Preview
Show the publishing tab and version history (do not publish on a shared environment)
scenes.narration: Website content is managed in the console. Pages, services, projects, stories, the gallery, testimonials and FAQs each have an editor built from the content's structure. Changes are saved as drafts, can be previewed on the real website through a private link, and are published immediately or on a schedule. Every save is kept in the version history, so an earlier version can be restored.
visualDirection: Split screen: editor left, preview right

scenes.title: Business administration
screenAction: Open Orders, filter by status, open an order: fulfilment steps
Open Products and Inventory: adjust stock with a reason
Open Employees and Attendance: daily board, corrections queue, leave queue
scenes.narration: Orders move through clear fulfilment steps, with refunds and cancellations recorded. Products, sizes and prices are edited in one place, and inventory changes always carry a reason, so stock history can be traced. For HR, the console holds employee records, work schedules, a daily attendance board, a corrections queue and leave approvals. Nobody can approve their own records.
visualDirection: Quick cuts between the four list pages
Zoom on the stock adjustment reason

scenes.title: Real-time updates
screenAction: Two browser windows side by side: admin Attendance (left), employee dashboard (right), two separate browser profiles
Employee presses Clock in
Admin board updates without a reload; the bell count changes
scenes.narration: Changes appear live. When an employee clocks in, the attendance board in the admin console updates on its own, without a page reload. The live connection only carries a short signal; the console then fetches the new data through the API, which checks the viewer's permissions again. If the connection drops, it reconnects and catches up.
visualDirection: Pulse highlight on the row that changes

scenes.title: Notifications
screenAction: Open the bell dropdown, then the notifications page
Show the preferences: categories, sounds, push toggle
scenes.narration: The admin console and the employee portal each have a notification centre with an unread count, categories and optional sounds, and customers get their own on the website. People choose which notifications they receive. Web Push can deliver them to the device when the portal is closed, once push keys are configured for the environment.

scenes.title: Technical architecture
screenAction: Show the overall architecture diagram from docs/architecture/diagrams.md
Show the admin System monitoring page
scenes.narration: Under the hood, the three portals are Next.js applications, and they talk to an Express API written in TypeScript. PostgreSQL holds orders, people and attendance, MongoDB holds the website content, and Redis provides caching and coordination. Supabase handles sign-in and file storage, and Socket.IO carries live updates. Each service runs in its own Docker container, and every change passes automated tests and security scans before it reaches production.
scenes.pronunciation: Supabase: SOO-pa-base; PostgreSQL: post-gres-Q-L; Redis: RED-iss
visualDirection: Cut to the System page with live health checks

scenes.title: Closing
screenAction: Return to the home page hero
Fade to the logo on white
scenes.narration: Greenscape now runs its website, shop, attendance and administration on one connected system. Customers get a clear way to explore and buy, employees get a simple daily tool, and the team gets one place to run the business. Thank you for watching.
